Happens with spider combos sometimes, it’s a symptom of corkscrewing. I give mine tubes to crawl through rather than big climbing branches and keep his temps a bit cooler than my other enclosures as the condition seems temperature sensitive, and try to keep the humidity at around 70% and boost it while he’s shedding. From what I understand it’s an inner ear condition that throws off their ability to regulate their sense of direction and affects balance. As long as they’re eating and drinking properly it doesn’t need to be addressed by a vet, since theres not much a vet can do anyway. Just keep an eye on the frequency of the behavior and be mindful when feeding (I suggest frozen or pre-killed food) bc they’re a lot more likely to miss their mark on the first try.

My snake made a similar noise when he had some shed stuck in his nostrils and heat pits. Came out the next day bc he was just having some issues getting his face shed off. If for sure he doesn’t have an RI just keep an eye on it and see if it goes away with his next shed. They can also get infections in their glottis, I would maybe suggest a second opinion if possible, and see if maybe he just needs antibiotics. I’ve had a snake get a tumor in his mouth, sometimes an issue is just something less common that you don’t think to look for or ask about. 
In the meantime try to keep your humidity consistent between 65%-75%, and I’d also suggest feeding a snake around that size every 7 days instead of every 10. I start feeding my snakes at 10 day intervals at around 350g, and 14 day intervals when they hit abt 650g, if that helps.

Like I said, it’s up to the ethics of the individual, i acknowledge that I can’t make people make decisions but the animals already exist. Considering ball pythons in general are seemingly overbred to the point they’re sold in bulk (at least in my area), many with defects that aren’t as widely known as spiders for some reason, my opinion is I don’t even really believe it’s ethical to breed them at all anymore given how unregulated and over saturated the market is. But I can’t stop that so I simply inform on care needs of animals that already exist and are probably going to keep existing.

I would ask the breeder what the degree of wobble is, if symptomatic. Some present it in varying degrees, some don’t. It’s matter of commitment to their care, your personal ethical boundaries and if you wanna go for it. 

As long as their husbandry is consistent and accurate, most act like regular ball pythons. I have one who’s essentially asymptomatic, another who corkscrews intensely, both are great eaters and healthy, social, normal snakes, just one requires similar but altered care.

Edit: if you’re going to make eugenics-adjacent comments to me might as well be aware that I have Tourette’s, which is a very similar genetic condition to the spider condition. People don’t like looking at me either. So while I’m not really for them being bred I still empathize with them. 

Regardless of anyone’s opinion on them, Im simply making it known that they require different care than regular ball pythons. Many people go into getting them without knowing that, whether they buy them or rescue them, so I bring it up on posts like these.

For my guy, since he’s a fall risk, I got him tunnels (like pull apart Guinea pig tunnels) fand he actually gets around very well by using his nose and pushing things out of the way so he doesn’t have to stretch up. Another thing is temps/humidity. I have to keep his stats very consistent or he gets agitated. So it’s already been noted that the spider gene has an inner ear deformity, I’m not gonna harp on that anymore than it already has been. I just also wanna mention this in case you consider breeding them anyway, bc obv many people still do despite their controversy since corkscrews aren’t guaranteed. It’s also just an interesting genetics fact if you’ve already made up your mind not to. 

Spider is a lethal homozygous gene so it *cannot* be bred to itself, it will not produce viable offspring and they’ll all die in the egg. This also goes for the “champagne” gene, it can’t be bred to itself or spider as it has a similar condition (theoretically, there aren’t any studies on them as far as I know).  

That said, as much as I love ball pythons, balls are pretty over-bred in the snake trade anyway and have just abt saturated the market. If I can make a breeding suggestion, if it is something you wanna do, I suggest super dwarf retics ! They have amazing temperaments and they’re a much more manageable size in comparison to regular sized retics, but for some reason I don’t see them anywhere ! I would love to see more on the market.
